# runr_runtime_source (Resource)

A runtime source ([runtime sources](https://runr.sh/docs/runtimes/#runtime-sources)): an OCI catalog of signed manifests (`kind = "oci-catalog"`) or a Git repository with `<path>/<id>/runtime.yaml` (`kind = "git"`), public or private, that RunR reads runtimes from — when it is connected or changed, every `interval_minutes` and when `sync_trigger` changes. A platform source (a token with `runtimes.manage`) gives every organization its runtimes; a source of the organization (`runtimes.use_custom`, while the platform allows custom runtimes) only its members.

A read that fails (`status` `unreachable`, `not_found`, `auth_failed`, `invalid_signature`, `invalid_catalog`) leaves the source's runtimes as they were and is a warning, not an error: the source is connected. A runtime manifest with problems is refused (`status = "partial"`, `problems` with file and JSON path), the others are read. Check the read with a `postcondition` on `status` where it must succeed.

The credentials are write-only: RunR never returns them (`credentials` says which are set). Terraform keeps what it set (`git_token`, `ssh_private_key`, `registry_password`, sensitive), or with the `_wo` attributes (Terraform 1.11 and later) nothing — change `credentials_wo_version` to write new ones. Credentials changed or removed outside Terraform are written again. Destroying the source deletes its runtimes no project uses; the others stay, orphaned, until their sunset. RunR's own catalog (the default source) is the installation's: read it with `data.runr_runtime_source`. Import with the source's id or name (the credentials are not imported).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A private Git repository of runtimes (runtimes/<id>/runtime.yaml on the main branch), read
# with an access token Terraform never stores (write-only, Terraform 1.11 and later).
variable "runtimes_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

resource "runr_runtime_source" "acme" {
  name                   = "acme-runtimes"
  kind                   = "git"
  url                    = "https://gitlab.example.com/acme/runtimes.git"
  ref                    = "main"
  git_token_wo           = var.runtimes_token
  credentials_wo_version = "2026-11" # change it to write a rotated token
  interval_minutes       = 30

  # Read the repository now when a new runtimes release is tagged.
  sync_trigger = "v1.4.0"

  lifecycle {
    postcondition {
      condition     = self.status == "ok"
      error_message = "RunR could not read every runtime of acme-runtimes (${self.status}): ${coalesce(self.error, "see problems")}"
    }
  }
}

# A signed OCI catalog in a private registry, with its patch feed.
resource "runr_runtime_source" "catalog" {
  name              = "acme-catalog"
  kind              = "oci-catalog"
  url               = "registry.example.com/acme/runtimes:catalog"
  public_key        = file("${path.module}/cosign.pub")
  patch_feed        = "registry.example.com/acme/runtimes:patches"
  registry_username = "runr"
  registry_password = var.registry_password
}

variable "registry_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Projects use a runtime of a source by its id.
resource "runr_project" "script" {
  name      = "nightly-report"
  type      = "xaas"
  runtime   = "bash"
  region_id = data.runr_region.eu.id

  depends_on = [runr_runtime_source.acme]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) `git` (a repository of `<path>/<id>/runtime.yaml`) or `oci-catalog` (a signed catalog of manifests).
- `name` (String) Name, unique in its scope (at most 64 characters).
- `url` (String) The repository (`https://…` or `git@host:owner/repo.git`) or the catalog's OCI reference (`registry/repo:tag`).

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `credentials_wo_version` (String) Any string; a change writes the `_wo` credentials again (for example a rotation date).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether RunR reads the source on its interval (default `true`); off, its runtimes stay as last read.
- `git_token` (String, Sensitive) `git` over HTTPS: access token (sensitive). One of `git_token`, `git_token_wo`, `ssh_private_key` and `ssh_private_key_wo` at most.
- `git_token_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) `git_token` that Terraform never stores (write-only, Terraform 1.11 and later); change `credentials_wo_version` to write a new one.
- `git_username` (String) `git` over HTTPS: user name of the token (default `x-access-token`).
- `interval_minutes` (Number) Minutes between reads: at least the platform's minimum (5 unless configured otherwise), at most a week. Left out: 60 for a new source, an existing one keeps its interval.
- `patch_feed` (String) OCI reference of the source's signed runtime patch feed (needs `public_key`).
- `path` (String) `git`: directory of the runtimes (default `runtimes`).
- `public_key` (String) cosign public key (PEM) the catalog and the patch feed must verify with, e.g. `file("cosign.pub")`.
- `ref` (String) `git`: branch, tag or commit (default the repository's default branch).
- `registry_host` (String) Registry the registry credentials are for (`ghcr.io`, `registry.example.com:5000`); required with registry credentials of a `git` source (the registry of its runtime images).
- `registry_password` (String, Sensitive) Registry password or token (sensitive).
- `registry_password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) `registry_password` that Terraform never stores (write-only, Terraform 1.11 and later); change `credentials_wo_version` to write a new one.
- `registry_username` (String) Registry user for a private catalog, patch feed or runtime images (with `registry_password` or `registry_password_wo`).
- `ssh_known_hosts` (String) `git` over SSH: `known_hosts` of the host; without it the host key is accepted on first use.
- `ssh_private_key` (String, Sensitive) `git` over SSH (`git@…` URL): the deploy key (sensitive), e.g. `file("deploy_key")`.
- `ssh_private_key_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) `ssh_private_key` that Terraform never stores (write-only, Terraform 1.11 and later); change `credentials_wo_version` to write a new one.
- `sync_trigger` (String) Any string; a change reads the source now (for example the tag or commit runtimes were released with). Every other change reads it as well.

### Read-Only

- `checked_at` (String) When RunR last read the source.
- `credentials` (Attributes) Which credentials the source has, as RunR reports them (never a value). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credentials))
- `error` (String) Why the last read failed.
- `id` (String) Source id.
- `problems` (Attributes List) The problems of the last read: `file`, `runtime`, `path` (JSON path in the manifest), `message`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--problems))
- `revision` (String) Catalog digest or commit of the last good read.
- `runtimes_count` (Number) Runtimes the source gives.
- `scope` (String) `platform` (connected with `runtimes.manage`: every organization) or `organization`.
- `signature_verified` (Boolean) The last read's catalog verified with `public_key`.
- `status` (String) The last read: `never`, `ok`, `partial` (some manifests refused: `problems`), `unreachable`, `not_found`, `auth_failed`, `invalid_signature`, `invalid_catalog` or `disabled`.
- `synced_at` (String) When the last good read was.

<a id="nestedatt--credentials"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credentials`

Read-Only:

- `git` (String) `token` (HTTPS), `ssh` (a deploy key) or null.
- `git_token_hint` (String) The token's last four characters behind a mask (tokens longer than eight characters).
- `git_username` (String) User name of the Git token (null: `x-access-token`).
- `known_hosts_set` (Boolean) `known_hosts` is set (without it the host key is accepted on first use).
- `registry_password_set` (Boolean) A registry password is set.
- `registry_username` (String) The registry user.
- `ssh_key_set` (Boolean) A deploy key is set.


<a id="nestedatt--problems"></a>
### Nested Schema for `problems`

Read-Only:

- `file` (String) The file (a Git source's `<path>/<id>/runtime.yaml`).
- `message` (String) The problem.
- `path` (String) JSON path in the manifest.
- `runtime` (String) The runtime id or directory.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <source id or name>. The credentials are not imported: the next apply writes the configured
# ones (with the _wo attributes, set credentials_wo_version). RunR's catalog cannot be imported.
terraform import runr_runtime_source.acme acme-runtimes
```
